steps.description: Registered session 1 (claude / claude-opus-5, high).

Replaced the binary disposition.uat (status walked|waived) with a per-component accounting: attestation + components[], each record carrying component, method (6-value vocabulary), reviewers ({type,count}, distinct humans), evidence, findings and a per-component attestation. Reviewer types and component keys are CLOSED vocabularies - the first makes 'an AI reviewed it' unrecordable (spec decision 9), the second makes a self-assessed confidence score or debt ledger unrecordable. Landed in disposition.py (constants + _validate_uat_block) and mirrored in disposition.schema.json ($defs UatComponentRecord / UatReviewer), which an existing parity test caught me not having done.

New spec key uatComponents parsed by spec_config (omitted vs explicitly-empty kept distinct, and the block-list scan cannot swallow the neighbouring prerequisites: list). check_uat_walk_recorded now reads it: an armed set with no inventory is REFUSED rather than defaulted inert, a declared component with no record is refused and named, an unmatched record is refused as a likely typo, and method 'none'/'not-applicable' with an attestation PASSES. Path-shaped evidence is checked for existence; URLs and free-text (SharePoint/Teams) are not. 61 new tests in test_set113_uat_accounting.py plus falsifiers in the schema parity suite; 280 targeted tests green.

Journaled under OPERATOR authority with the operator's own words from operator-notes.md 2026-08-10 as the attestation. First attempted the same record under authority='ai', which decision_journal refused (exit 5, verification-reduction carve-out) - the refusal the spec calls correct, exercised rather than assumed. A second decision journals the mid-set addition of uatComponents to this set's own spec.
**Cross-provider verification.**
**Required portion of the full test suite.**
**Close-out.**
Registered session 2 (claude / claude-opus-5, high).

Defined the portable scenario model in ai_router/scenario.py: stable kebab-case scenario and step ids, prerequisites, baseline (description/setup/observable), reset, recovery, named checkpoints, and per step an action plus an expected observable result. Closed vocabularies at both levels -- an unknown key is refused, not ignored.

Quarantined driver detail structurally: drivers: is opaque to the model, no renderer receives it, and portable_digest() is taken over the portable half only, so a selector change leaves all four renderings byte-identical. ai_router/scenario_lint.py is the advisory second line for selector-shaped text that leaks into portable prose; five rules, each with a planted violation and a legitimate look-alike.

Rendered four documents from the one source (walkthrough.md, training.md, captions.vtt, chapters.json) via ai_router/scenario_render.py, with --check as the divergence gate over the committed tree. Both prose documents state verbatim that no video is needed and carry the replay rule: reaching any step means replaying a prefix from the baseline or the nearest named checkpoint, never random access. One exemplar authored: docs/walkthroughs/work-explorer-first-look.

Four rounds, all routed to gpt-5-6-sol with anthropic excluded. Discovery fan-out (2 lenses) + supplementary found 3 Majors and 8 nits; remediation-review cycle 1 REJECTED one fix (the CSS-id rule missed button#save) and cycle 2 returned VERIFIED with 3 fix verdicts accepted. One nit disputed with deterministic evidence: byte comparison would fail --check on every Windows clone. $1.90.

All three declared suites run after the last code-changing stage: pytest 4893 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (228s, run at -n 8 per the operator parallelism cap rather than the declared -n auto, recorded in the run's detail field); mocha 1468 passing (23s); playwright 32 passed (180s) on an idle machine. All three recorded via run_of_record.
**Close-out.**
Registered session 3 (claude / claude-opus-5).

Built the fixture web app (src/test/fixtures/task-board: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, served over HTTP on an ephemeral port by scripts/web-fixture-server.js) as the stand-in for the .NET/Java/vanilla-JS/Python web targets, which are one platform, not four. Reproduced browser recordVideo WITH A CONTROL by the same method Set 111 S4 used to measure the workbench failure: the same fixed probe run twice, differing only in whether recordVideo was passed. Arm A (passed) drove the UI and wrote a 30374-byte video; arm B (omitted) drove the UI and wrote nothing - the exact inversion of the workbench table. Recorded raw in s3-browser-record-measurement.json and reproducible via scripts/measure-browser-record.js, which exits non-zero if the premise ever stops holding. The video is .webm, not MP4, which is the first evidence for the manifest requirement in step 3.

Shipped ai_router/walkthrough_run.py: a JSONL step-event stream (run-started / started / completed / failed / run-finished) keyed by S2's stable step ids, and an artifact-agnostic run manifest. The parser is lenient about truncation (a killed driver's half-written last line is dropped with a note) and strict about contradiction (unknown kind, out-of-order timestamp, terminal event for a step that never started, a stepId the scenario does not declare). Artifact kinds are a closed vocabulary that names terminal-cast and transcript alongside video, every artifact carries an explicit mediaType, an EMPTY artifact list is valid, and a listed-but-missing file is refused. Timing is anchored honestly: the driver brackets newContext() and reports the width of the bracket as anchor.uncertaintyMillis (6-7ms measured) rather than implying frame accuracy. Caption retiming reuses the existing VTT writer via a windows_ms parameter instead of a second copy - measured drift on the real run was ~0.6s cumulative against the authored estimates. Chapter mapping is the manifest's per-step startMillis/endMillis, so there is no second chapters schema to drift. Per the operator's 2026-08-15 tier-2 hedge, each step's target bounding box is recorded and read by nothing.

One command (npm run walkthrough:web -> scripts/record-web-walkthrough.js) drives the fixture, records it, and produces a watchable captioned result in gitignored .walkthrough-runs/. The driver does NOT parse scenario.yaml - walkthrough_run plan hands it the portable steps plus its own quarantined block as JSON, so the repo keeps one scenario parser. Real run: 5/5 steps, 44.1s, 944KB webm, retimed captions, self-contained index.html. Both degraded paths proven, not asserted: --no-video produces a manifest with no video, an index that says so where the player would be, and no captions sidecar; a planted failing expectation in step 3 yields outcome=failed with steps 4-5 recorded as not-reached rather than absent. Cleanup is deterministic and ordered (events stream, context, browser, server, scratch video dir, each guarded); the output dir is emptied per run but REFUSES a non-empty --out that is not a prior run. Tier-1 emphasis outlines the target and dims the rest, injected by the driver so it works against an app that cannot be edited - and it is released after the action, which a first recording proved necessary: the fixture re-renders its list, destroying the emphasised node and leaving the page grey for the rest of the step.

Four rounds, all routed to gpt-5-6-sol with anthropic excluded. ROUND 1 VERIFIED NOTHING: the work had been committed first and verify_session diffs the working tree against HEAD, so the bundle was empty; both findings correctly said so, but with only spec.md to cite the doc-only cap recorded them at Minor and the round printed 'MINOR-ONLY ... effectively VERIFIED' with instructions to close. Round 2 (--diff-base at the pre-session ref) reviewed the real 4681-line delta and found 1 Critical + 4 Majors = 3 distinct defects, all accepted, none disputed, all sharing one shape: each worked on the bundled fixture and failed on a real consumer app. Round 3 (remediation-review) returned VERIFIED, 3 fix verdicts accepted / 0 rejected, and explicitly resolved the round-1 findings. Round 4 is the A4 delta-scoped review owed because docs/walkthroughs/README.md - classified as shipped, correctly - changed after round 3; also VERIFIED, 0 findings. The round-1 hole was fixed at source rather than by weakening the operator-attested severity cap. $2.2754 across 8 routed calls, stated without netting out the $0.44 that bought no verification.

All three declared suites run to completion after the last code-changing edit and recorded via run_of_record: pytest 4978 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (235s, at -n 8 per the operator parallelism cap rather than the declared -n auto); mocha 1492 passing (17s, +24 for the new webWalkthroughRecorder suite); playwright 37 passed (180s, +5 for expectation-wait.spec.ts). Layer 3 is owed by this session's own spec step 6 and by L-064-12, since package.json counts as product. The FIRST full pytest run found 5 failures - every one a fixture artifact of the new empty-evidence guard, in files not previously run - so they were fixed and the WHOLE suite re-run rather than re-running the five, which is the point of the policy.
**Close-out.**
